## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Sāmisa* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 55) is a training rule (*sekhiya-dhamma*) for Buddhist monks preserved within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Rendered by Bhikkhu Sujato as "Receiving with soiled hand" and translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali, the rule concerns proper monastic decorum when accepting or handling food and monastic requisites [SuttaCentral].

This training rule represents an ancient core Vinaya observance with extensive cross-sectarian attestations. SuttaCentral identifies parallels throughout the surviving Vinaya literature of various schools, including the Pali Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, Vibhaṅgas, and Parivāras, as well as the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus registers 270 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 94 texts, exhibiting dense formulaic sharing with adjacent etiquette rules such as Sekhiya 56 (§1.4–1.26), Sekhiya 37, and Sekhiya 57, as well as other Vibhaṅga and Khandhaka contexts including Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3, Pācittiya 35, and the Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka (Kd 15) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the rule across languages with the Tibetan translation of the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104-2) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
